title: Profiling of rRNA-derived small RNAs in Arabidopsis thaliana using rsRNAfinder
author: Kalakoti, Vivek, et al.

steps.title: Select Arabidopsis sRNA‑seq datasets
steps.instruction: Choose Col‑0 tissue libraries (flower, fruit, leaf, shoot, seed, root) with >1 million mapped reads; record accession details (see Table S1).

steps.title: Trim reads with TrimGalore
steps.instruction: Run TrimGalore v0.0.4 on raw reads applying a minimum quality score of 20.

steps.title: Align reads with Segemehl
steps.instruction: Align trimmed reads to TAIR10 genome using Segemehl with options -D 2 -M 50, allowing 1–3 nucleotide mismatches and a maximum mismatch rate of 5 %.

steps.title: Identify rsRNA loci
steps.instruction: For each rRNA locus, determine the predominant read sequence to define rsRNAs.

steps.title: Search snoRNA modifications
steps.instruction: Query the snOPY database for snoRNA‑based modification sites on target rRNAs to find rsRNAs that retain modifications.

steps.title: Predict rsRNA target genes
steps.instruction: Use psRNATarget with Araport11 transcripts, Schema V2 settings, and retain only the top two hits per target.

steps.title: Perform pathway enrichment
steps.instruction: Conduct functional enrichment analysis on the predicted rsRNA‑targeting genes.

steps.title: Validate targets with Cleaveland
steps.instruction: Run Cleaveland v4.5 (default parameters) on PARE‑Seq datasets GSM1263708 (flower), GSM1330569 (leaf), and GSM3321205 (seedling) to confirm rsRNA‑target interactions.

steps.title: Obtain mutant sRNA‑seq libraries
steps.instruction: Download publicly available sRNA‑seq libraries from dcl, rrp6l, and fry mutants and corresponding wild‑type samples (see Table S2).

steps.title: Trim and align mutant libraries
steps.instruction: Trim and align mutant and wild‑type reads using the same TrimGalore and Segemehl parameters described in steps 2‑3.

steps.title: Interpret mutant rsRNA results
steps.instruction: Use the output files from step 10 for downstream comparative analysis of rsRNA expression in mutants versus wild‑type.
